# Conformance suite

21 synthetic DPA descriptions in [`tests/fixtures/`](../tests/fixtures/), each with the review state, exit code and open rules the CLI must produce, recorded in [`expected.json`](../tests/fixtures/expected.json). [`tests/test_conformance.py`](../tests/test_conformance.py) runs every fixture through the CLI on every push, on Python 3.10 to 3.14, and fails on any difference.

The fixtures freeze what the rules do today. Where a result looks legally questionable it is flagged below for review rather than changed: a rule change needs a lawyer's sign-off and a deliberate update of the expected result.

## ⚑ Flagged for legal review

- **`02-adequacy-only.json`**: Changed input: the fixture now records the facts the Japanese decision's scope turns on (recipient_type private_commercial, scope_carve_out none). Without them the transfer to Japan is NEEDS_REVIEW (HIGH) and the packet BLOCKED (fixture 17), because an unknown adequacy condition never counts as adequacy (owner's answer of 10 November 2026). Reading a private commercial organisation as a personal information handling business operator rests on recital 32 of Implementing Decision (EU) 2019/419 and is an interpretation.
- **`04-sccs-without-tia.json`**: Changed: Article 1 of Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795 covers only organisations on the Data Privacy Framework List, so SCCs recorded for a US importer now get the scope question every destination with a scope-limited adequacy decision gets. transfer.us asks whether the importer is on that list for the data transferred and, if not, for a transfer impact assessment; it is MEDIUM until one is recorded and replaces the generic transfer.impact_assessment finding. The review state is unchanged. Confirm the changed expected result.
- **`05-dpf-us-importer.json`**: Changed by PR #4: the DPF is treated as an Art. 45 adequacy decision (Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795), not an Art. 46 safeguard, so a transfer to an importer recorded as actively certified on the Data Privacy Framework List for the data transferred is PRESENT and asks for no transfer impact assessment. The fixture now records that certification and the data it covers. Confirm the changed expected result.
- **`06-art49-derogation.json`**: Changed by PR #4: a derogation not recorded as occasional and not repetitive is treated like a missing basis (HIGH), so this fixture is now BLOCKED instead of NEEDS_REVIEW (MEDIUM). EDPB Guidelines 2/2018, section 1, read the derogations restrictively. Confirm the changed expected result.
- **`07-vague-breach-timing.json`**: Any timing wording without "undue delay" or "without delay" (also "within 24 hours") is an open HIGH finding and blocks the packet. Confirm that this is the intended threshold.
- **`10-brazil-adequacy.json`**: Changed: Brazil is now in the adequacy reference data under Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/179 of 26 January 2026 (OJ L, 2026/179, 28.1.2026), read on EUR-Lex on 2026-11-10, so the transfer is PRESENT and the packet CLEARED_FOR_REVIEW instead of BLOCKED. Article 1 of the decision covers only controllers and processors in Brazil subject to the LGPD; the finding states that scope for the reviewer. The input records no fact for that limit: the tool reads every importer in Brazil as subject to the LGPD (interpretation, owner's answer of 10 November 2026) and asks the reviewer to confirm it.
- **`16-canada-public-body.json`**: Decision 2002/2/EC covers recipients subject to PIPEDA (Art. 1); recital 5 says the Act does not apply to organisations under the Federal Privacy Act or the provincial public sector. Reading a public body as outside the decision is an interpretation (owner's answer of 10 November 2026: private-sector scope, a non-profit goes to review).
- **`17-japan-carve-out-not-recorded.json`**: An unknown adequacy condition is NEEDS_REVIEW with HIGH severity, so the packet is BLOCKED until the carve-out is recorded (owner's answer of 10 November 2026). It was CLEARED_FOR_REVIEW before scope conditions were modelled.
- **`20-review-date-before-uk-amendment.json`**: A review date before an amendment that changed the decision's scope or validity is a review state (NEEDS_REVIEW, HIGH): the tool models only the decision as last amended (owner's answer of 10 November 2026). The amendment is dated by its adoption (interpretation).

Run the suite with `make test`, or a single fixture with `dpa-review --input tests/fixtures/<name> --quiet; echo $?`.
